media.proposal.clears: {bank}: clears {count, plural, one {# detected region} other {# detected regions}}.

@media.proposal.clears.context: First line of a code-detection proposal in clear mode (the ann-detect / skool-import command output and result document): how many regions the detector wrote before will be reset.

placeholders.bank: The bank's name as the proposal lists it, e.g. 'bank 5' or 'ROM'

media.proposal.summary: {bank}: code {code, number} (observed {observed, number}, reached {reached, number}, inferred {inferred, number}), data {data, number}, unknown {unknown, number} ({percent, number}%). {changes, plural, one {# change} other {# changes}}, {conflicts, plural, one {# conflict} other {# conflicts}} with your regions.

@media.proposal.summary.context: Summary line of a code-detection proposal for one memory bank (command output and result document). The byte counts are per class: code (split by evidence: seen executed, reached by following jumps, inferred), data, and still unknown bytes with their share of the bank. 'Your regions' are regions the user marked by hand.

placeholders.bank: The bank's name as the proposal lists it, e.g. 'bank 5' or 'ROM'
placeholders.reached: Code bytes reached by following control flow
placeholders.percent: Share of the bank still unknown, e.g. 12.5
placeholders.changes: Number of changes applying would make
placeholders.conflicts: Number of user regions the detection disagrees with

@media.proposal.yoursMarker.context: Marker at the end of a proposal row (a monospace listing) that changes a region the user created by hand.

@media.proposal.conflict.context: Row of a detection proposal listing (monospace): a region the user marked by hand that detection disagrees with; it is kept unchanged.

placeholders.yours: The user's region type, e.g. 'data' (an annotation type keyword; not translated)
placeholders.detected: The detected region type, e.g. 'disassemble' (keyword; not translated)

@media.proposal.note.context: Row of a detection proposal listing (monospace): notes about a run of bytes (self-modifying code, the stack, the screen, interrupt code).

placeholders.notes: Comma-separated note codes, e.g. 'smc, stack' (not translated)

@media.proposal.warning.context: Row of a detection proposal listing (monospace): a warning the classifier raised at an address.

media.proposal.moreWarnings: ... {count, plural, one {# more warning} other {# more warnings}}

@media.proposal.moreWarnings.context: Last row of a detection proposal listing when there were more than 20 warnings: how many are not listed.

media.annotations.machineMismatch: These annotations were written for the {file} bank space; this machine numbers its memory as {current}. Labels may name the wrong bytes.

@media.annotations.machineMismatch.context: Warning when an annotation set (a sidecar file of labels and comments) is opened on a different machine than the one it was written for.

placeholders.file: Bank-space id the file was written for, e.g. 'next' (not translated)
placeholders.current: Bank-space id of the current machine, e.g. 'sp128' (not translated)

media.annotations.chunkNotAnnotatable: This memory (a DOCK or EXROM chunk) cannot be annotated.

media.romExport.identical: Verified: the source assembles to the ROM, byte for byte ({bytes, plural, one {# byte} other {# bytes}}).

@media.romExport.identical.context: Result of exporting a ROM's annotations as Klive Z80 source (the ROM annotation editor's 'Export as source' row and the rom-ann-export command output): the exported file was assembled with Klive's assembler and compared with the ROM. Success.

media.romExport.notAssembled: Not verified: the source does not assemble (line {line}: {message}).

@media.romExport.notAssembled.context: Result of exporting a ROM's annotations as Klive Z80 source (the ROM annotation editor's 'Export as source' row and the rom-ann-export command output): the exported file was assembled with Klive's assembler and compared with the ROM. The assembler reported an error.

placeholders.line: Line number in the exported file

media.romExport.notChecked: Not verified: the source could not be assembled ({message}).

@media.romExport.notChecked.context: Result of exporting a ROM's annotations as Klive Z80 source (the ROM annotation editor's 'Export as source' row and the rom-ann-export command output): the exported file was assembled with Klive's assembler and compared with the ROM. The assembler could not be run at all.

media.romExport.different: Not verified: the source assembles to different bytes: {differences}.

@media.romExport.different.context: Result of exporting a ROM's annotations as Klive Z80 source (the ROM annotation editor's 'Export as source' row and the rom-ann-export command output): the exported file was assembled with Klive's assembler and compared with the ROM. The output differs from the ROM; the list names the first differing bytes.

placeholders.differences: Comma-separated list of media.romExport.byteDiffers / pageMoved items

@media.romExport.byteDiffers.context: One item of the media.romExport.different list: a byte of the assembled output that differs from the ROM. '--' stands for a missing byte.

placeholders.offset: Hex offset in the page, e.g. '$0D04'

@media.romExport.pageMoved.context: One item of the media.romExport.different list: a ROM page's code is assembled at the wrong address.

media.romExport.noPages: None of the ROM pages the annotations name were found, so there is nothing to export.

@media.romExport.noPages.context: Error of exporting a ROM's annotations as source (the ROM annotation editor and rom-ann-export): no ROM bytes match the sidecar's pages.

@media.sourceExport.dialogTitle.context: Export as source started from the UI (the Disassembly view's and a bank document's export button, their tools menu, Debug › Export Disassembly as Source…). Title of the save-file dialog and of the message box with the result.

@media.sourceExport.filter.context: Export as source started from the UI (the Disassembly view's and a bank document's export button, their tools menu, Debug › Export Disassembly as Source…). File-type filter name in the save dialog (files ending .kz80.asm or .asm).

media.sourceExport.buttonTitle: Export as source: write the listing as a Klive Z80 assembly file and check that it assembles to the same bytes

@media.sourceExport.buttonTitle.context: Export as source started from the UI (the Disassembly view's and a bank document's export button, their tools menu, Debug › Export Disassembly as Source…). Tooltip of the export icon button in the listing's header.

@media.sourceExport.verified.context: Export as source started from the UI (the Disassembly view's and a bank document's export button, their tools menu, Debug › Export Disassembly as Source…). Message box after an export whose file assembles to the same bytes. A blank line separates the file from the verdict.

placeholders.file: Full path of the exported file
placeholders.verdict: The export command's verdict, e.g. 'Verified: the export assembles to the same bytes.'

@media.sourceExport.notVerified.context: Export as source started from the UI (the Disassembly view's and a bank document's export button, their tools menu, Debug › Export Disassembly as Source…). Message box (an error) after an export that could not be written, or whose file does not assemble or assembles to different bytes.

placeholders.file: Full path of the chosen file
placeholders.verdict: The export command's message: why it failed, or the first differing bytes

media.sourceExport.noResult: The export command did not answer.

@media.sourceExport.noResult.context: Export as source started from the UI (the Disassembly view's and a bank document's export button, their tools menu, Debug › Export Disassembly as Source…). Shown in the result message box when the IDE returned nothing.

media.export.wrapsAsDefb: {address}: {instruction} is written as .defb (the jump wraps round $FFFF, which the assembler does not accept).

@media.export.wrapsAsDefb.context: Note after export-asm: a relative jump near the top of memory reaches its target only because the Z80 wraps the address round $FFFF; the assembler rejects such a distance, so its bytes are written instead.
